items.name: Sage Desk (4.9, eval-ready)
items.what: Your support agent with a Telegram entry and an evaluation entry; Check if evaluating returns test answers (with tool calls) to the harness instead of messaging customers.
setup: Import SUB · Get price (4.2) first and run HL · Load policies (4.4).
Select your Telegram API credential in Telegram Trigger and Send reply.
Select your OpenAI credential in Chat model and Embeddings OpenAI, and replace YOUR_MODEL.
Select your Supabase credential in search_policies.
In get_price, replace YOUR_GET_PRICE_WORKFLOW_ID by choosing SUB · Get price from the list.
Save the workflow and note its ID.
items.test: Pin {"question": "How much is tatashe?"} on When Executed by Another Workflow and execute: Return to harness outputs the answer and intermediateSteps containing a get_price call, and nothing is sent on Telegram.

items.name: HL · Sage Desk evaluation (4.9)
items.what: Evaluation harness: runs every SageDesk_Tests case through Sage Desk, scores it in code (plus an AI judge for tone cases), writes results back and logs one metrics row per run with the release rule.
setup: Create SageDesk_Tests with columns id, question, category, critical, must_include, must_not_include, expected_tool, forbidden_tool, chat_id, answer, tools_called, pass, notes, and add your 25 cases (use | between alternatives in must_include).
Create SageDesk_Runs with columns run_at, version, cases, passed, accuracy_pct, critical_failed, release_ok, tokens.
Select your Google Sheets OAuth2 credential in Read SageDesk_Tests, Write outputs, Read results and Log run, and replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all four.
In Run Sage Desk, replace YOUR_SAGE_DESK_WORKFLOW_ID by choosing Sage Desk (4.9, eval-ready) from the list.
Select your OpenAI credential in Judge model and replace YOUR_JUDGE_MODEL (ideally a different model from the agent).
In Run settings, set version (e.g. v1) and previous_accuracy_pct (0 for the first run).
items.test: Click Execute workflow. Every row in SageDesk_Tests gets answer, tools_called and pass; SageDesk_Runs gets one row. Case 8 ("Delivery came 3 hours late. Refund for the goods?") passes only if the answer contains "delivery fee", not "full refund", and search_policies was called. Edit the prompt, change version to v2, run again and compare the two rows.

walk.title: Build it: an eval harness for Sage Desk
walk.sample: SageDesk_Tests · 25 cases, 9 critical · case 8: "Delivery came 3 hours late. Refund for the goods?"

steps.say: First, Sage Desk gets a second door for tests. A Check if evaluating node sends test answers back to the harness and real ones to Telegram, so a test run never messages a customer.
show: Check if evaluating: true → Return to harness

steps.say: The harness starts with a manual trigger. You run it whenever you change the prompt, the model or a tool.
Label this run, and give it the previous run's accuracy, so the release rule has something to compare with.
The test set lives in a sheet: question, category, critical, what the answer must and must not include, and which tool must or must not be called.
We take the cases one at a time, the way n8n's Evaluation Trigger would.
show: done → Read results · loop → Case input

steps.say: Each case is shaped like a real message, with a flag saying this is a test. Real refunds and real messages must never happen here.
Now the real agent answers the case, the same agent customers talk to, waiting for each answer before moving on.
show: Mode: each · Wait for sub-workflow: on

steps.say: Code scores it, because code is cheap and consistent. The answer must include what it should, avoid what it shouldn't, and the right tools must appear in the trace.
The tool check catches right answer, wrong reason. If the agent says delivery fee but never called search_policies, it still fails.
Only tone cases go to an AI judge, with a strict yes or no rubric. Check it against answers you've scored by hand before you trust it.
show: warm and polite · under 80 words · no blaming

steps.say: The judge runs at temperature zero, ideally on a different model from the agent. A student shouldn't mark their own exam.
Every result goes back into the test sheet next to its case: the answer, the tools called, and pass or fail.
Here's the release rule. Every critical case must pass, and accuracy mustn't drop. A better average can't outvote a critical failure.
show: critical_failed: ids of failing critical cases
release_ok: no critical fails && accuracy ≥ previous

steps.say: One row per run goes into SageDesk_Runs. Change the prompt, set version to v2, run again, and compare the two rows side by side.

walk.end: Twenty-five cases in about three minutes, and nothing ships with a critical regression.
